title: Worry after unprotected sex
answer: Feeling scared after sex without a condom is very common, and worrying will not change what happened, but acting quickly can help. Within a few days, a health center can talk with you about emergency contraception, testing for HIV and other infections, and medicine that can prevent HIV if you go very soon. Try to slow your breathing and talk to someone you trust. You are not a bad person. You can also call 114 for free, private advice about what to do next.

title: Waiting for a pregnancy test result
answer: Waiting to find out if you are pregnant can feel very stressful. Remember that a test is most accurate from the day your period is late, so testing too early can give a wrong answer. A nurse at the health center can do a test and explain your choices kindly and privately. Whatever the result, you do not have to face it alone.

title: What a panic attack feels like
answer: A panic attack is a sudden wave of strong fear. Your heart may race, you may shake, sweat, feel short of breath, dizzy, or feel that something terrible is happening. It is very frightening but usually passes within minutes and is not dangerous by itself. Breathing slowly and reminding yourself it will pass can help. If attacks keep happening, talk to a health worker or counsellor. If you have chest pain or cannot breathe, get urgent care or call 112.

title: Calm breathing exercise
answer: Slow breathing tells your body it is safe. Sit comfortably and put a hand on your belly. Breathe in gently through your nose while you count to four, feeling your belly rise. Hold for a moment, then breathe out slowly through your mouth while you count to six. Repeat for a few minutes. You can do this before an exam, a test result or whenever you feel tense. Practising every day makes it work better.

title: Grounding when worry feels overwhelming
answer: Grounding brings your mind back to the present when worries feel too big. Try the 5-4-3-2-1 game: name 5 things you can see, 4 you can touch, 3 you can hear, 2 you can smell and 1 you can taste. You can also press your feet into the floor, hold something cool, or describe the room out loud. These simple steps help calm racing thoughts. If worry often feels overwhelming, talk to someone you trust or call 114.

If periods stay irregular for several months, see a nurse at the health center.

title: How much sleep young people need
answer: Teenagers usually need about 8 to 10 hours of sleep each night, and young adults about 7 to 9 hours. Your body grows, repairs itself and balances hormones while you sleep, and your brain stores what you learned. To sleep better, go to bed and wake up at similar times, avoid caffeine in the evening, put your phone away before bed, and keep your room dark and quiet.

answer: Not sleeping enough affects your whole body. It can make you moody, worried or irritable, lower your concentration and memory, weaken your immune system, and make you want sugary food. If you sleep badly for weeks despite good habits, talk to a health worker.

title: Caffeine, energy drinks and sleep
answer: Coffee, strong tea, cola and energy drinks contain caffeine, which keeps you awake. Energy drinks often contain a lot of caffeine and sugar. Avoid them in the afternoon and evening, and do not mix energy drinks with alcohol, which can hide how drunk you are. Water and good sleep are better ways to have energy.

title: Bedwetting as a teenager
answer: Some teenagers still wet the bed sometimes. It is more common than people think and it is not your fault or a sign of laziness. It can run in families or be linked to deep sleep, bladder development, constipation, stress or sometimes an illness such as an infection or diabetes. Empty your bladder before bed and avoid lots of drinks late at night. A health worker can check for causes and help, so please do not be ashamed to ask.

title: What self-esteem means
answer: Self-esteem is how you see and value yourself. Healthy self-esteem means you believe you are worthy of respect, even with weaknesses. Self-esteem is not fixed; it can grow with practice, support and kind thoughts about yourself.
